description: SAS datasets on the Warehouse research data platform, addressed and queried through the SAS engine. Currently the platform's only query context; a future non-SAS store there (e.g. a parquet lake) registers as its own system.
The CMS enterprise data warehouse (EDW).

OCS Medicare fee-for-service claim data as Warehouse works with it — SAS datasets, organized by claim form family into institutional (CMS-1450) and non_institutional (CMS-1500) schemas, each holding a claim-segment-level table (clm_sgmt) and a line-level table (clm_line).
notes: Bootstrapped from the origin system's layout reference.

description: The CMS enterprise data warehouse (EDW) production database. Hosts the presentation view layer presentation schemas — the governed view layers through which EDW data is accessed — across CMS programs, including Medicare, Medicaid, and Medicare-Medicaid (Medi-Medi).

Professional (noninstitutional) claims billed on the CMS-1500 form — the Professional (carrier) and DME file settings. Tables are unions across the settings; the 'Applicable file settings:' prefix on each column description lists which settings carry it.

The Medicare presentation view layer presentation schema: the view layer over EDW Medicare data, spanning beneficiary and enrollment, claims, provider, contract/plan, drug, geography, and code-set reference subject areas.
Line-level SAS dataset of professional (CMS-1500) claims — one row per line item (service line). Claim-level fields are repeated on every line row.

Claim-segment-level SAS dataset of professional (CMS-1500) claims — one row per claim segment. A segment holds up to 13 line items; a claim with more lines spans multiple segments (see sgmt_num, sgmt_cnt), but for the vast majority of claims one segment = one claim. Line and trailer fields appear as numbered wide columns.

A request for payment for health care services and/or products that were provided to a beneficiary by a Health Care Provider. This claim master has a number of subtypes that provide additional details specific to certain types of claims, such as Medicare Part A, Part B, Part D.
A detail claim line information pertaining to payment for healthcare service and/or products that were provided to a beneficiary by a Health Care Provider.

Claim type codes (CLM_TYPE_CD) — one row per code with its description, section-derived program family / source stream attributes, and the Warehouse crosswalk classifications (service type/category, program code, program type rollup, OCS file setting). The code identifies which source stream and claim type a claim row came from; consuming columns (edwc_prd clm_type_cd, ocs clm.clm_type) link here via `ref_table` so a consumer can resolve any code value.
notes: Provenance: the source data dictionary combined with the Warehouse claims-concepts reference (classification attributes, Medicare families only). Hand-maintained in the committed codes CSV (the source of truth; git is the history). Neither source carries effective/obsolete dating, so the set is undated.

join_condition: edwc_prd.claims_vw_prd.v_clm.geo_mbr_sk = edwc_prd.claims_vw_prd.v_clm_line.geo_mbr_sk and edwc_prd.claims_vw_prd.v_clm.clm_dt_grp_sk = edwc_prd.claims_vw_prd.v_clm_line.clm_dt_grp_sk and edwc_prd.claims_vw_prd.v_clm.clm_type_cd = edwc_prd.claims_vw_prd.v_clm_line.clm_type_cd and edwc_prd.claims_vw_prd.v_clm.clm_num_sk = edwc_prd.claims_vw_prd.v_clm_line.clm_num_sk and edwc_prd.claims_vw_prd.v_clm.clm_from_dt = edwc_prd.claims_vw_prd.v_clm_line.clm_from_dt
notes: 4-part key plus clm_from_dt (the required 5th condition for this one-to-many join). Omitting clm_from_dt risks associating line services with the wrong claim episode. Always filter clm_type_cd (and clm_from_dt when possible) on both sides.

label: Final-action restriction in the OCS extracts
definition: Teams query OCS data through a workbook that typically restricts the  pull to final-action claims, so the SAS datasets are typically  final-action only: one record per claim segment rather than a chain of adjustment and cancellation versions of the same claim. This is a property of how the extracts are produced, not of the national claims record layout. Where an extract does carry non-final-action claims, fa_drop is the field that differentiates them — a Warehouse-assigned claim-level flag marking the claims dropped by Warehouse's final-action selection algorithm.

label: Beneficiary external identifiers (MBI, HICN, RRB)
definition: The MBI (11-position, randomly assigned) replaced the HICN on Medicare cards and transactions (mandatory since January 2020). The legacy HICN is a 9-digit claim account number (CAN, the primary wage earner's account) plus a 1-2 position beneficiary identification code (BIC, the person's relationship to that wage earner) — so life events (spouse turning 65, divorce, remarriage) change a person's HICN. Railroad Retirement Board beneficiaries can carry two additional HICN formats (external alpha-prefix and internal). v_mbr_id_trkng tracks every identifier with mbr_id_type_cd (M/H/I/R), and cross-reference columns record identifier changes so any historical ID resolves to the current mbr_sk.

label: Claim Product deep vs. materialized wide
definition: Diagnosis and procedure codes are exposed in two shapes. v_clm_prod is DEEP: one code per row, differentiated by clm_prod_type_cd (P = principal, D = diagnosis, E = external cause, R = reason for visit) and clm_val_sqnc_num; it is the complete code list and lets a search condition be written once, at the cost of more rows. v_clm_prod_mtrlzd is WIDE: one row per claim with each code instance as its own column (clm_prncpl_dgns_cd, clm_dgns_1_cd,...); it holds most (not all) codes and requires checking every column in WHERE clauses. Institutional claims carry up to 25 diagnosis codes; professional claims up to 12.

label: Claim table taxonomy
definition: Column placement across the claim views follows a four-tier taxonomy. Primary common views (v_clm, v_clm_line) harmonize all claim streams and hold the frequently used columns. Common subset views split by service type (clm_instnl/clm_prfnl and their line equivalents) and exist to expose additional type-specific columns. Source-specific views (e.g. clm_strm_a, clm_strm_b tables) hold elements unique to one claim stream. Documentation (dcmtn) views hold infrequently used columns, split out for performance. Encounter/Duals-only columns live in the enctr views.

label: Four-part claim key
definition: The universal row identity across the Medicare view claim views is the 4-part key geo_mbr_sk + clm_dt_grp_sk + clm_type_cd + clm_num_sk; every claim-view join is built on it. One-to-one joins (header to header-subset views, line to line-subset views) use the 4-part key alone, adding clm_line_num for line-to-line joins. One-to-many joins require a 5th condition: clm_from_dt for header-to-line, or a type/sequence code for the code-list views. Joining without the required 5th condition silently associates unrelated services and produces misleading results. The 4-part key identifies one claim transaction, not the logical claim: each version in an adjustment chain has its own 4-part key, so an adjusted claim exists under multiple keys. To group versions into one logical claim, see claim_family_and_effective_key.

label: GPI drug classification hierarchy
definition: The Generic Product Identifier (GPI) classifies drugs hierarchically: the first two digits are the drug group (e.g. 65 = opioid analgesics), then classification/class (6510 opioid agonists, 6599 combinations), down to dosage form and strength. In the NDC views this surfaces as ndc_gpi_grp_cd/_desc, ndc_gpi_clsfctn_cd/_desc, ndc_gpi_dsg_form_cd, ndc_gpi_stgth_cd, and ndc_gpi_gnrc_name; the same family filter can be expressed via the group code or a prefix of the strength code.

label: NDC reference validity dating
definition: NDC codes are not indefinitely valid: manufacturers retire and reuse codes, so NDC reference joins must band the claim service date between ndc_efctv_dt and ndc_obslt_dt to select the code version valid at time of service — the same effective/obsolete time-band pattern used across the EDW. Skipping the band silently associates claims with the wrong drug version.

label: NPI column conventions on claim views
definition: The Medicare view has 70+ NPI columns. Columns prefixed clm_ hold the NPI as submitted on the source claim; columns prefixed prvdr_ hold an NPI obtained by lookup against the provider views. Provider-role population varies by claim program type: billing NPIs apply to all types except Part D, prescribers only to Part D (and there in the generic-id column clm_prsbng_prvdr_gnrc_id_num, not an NPI-named column), and rendering NPIs are consistently populated at the line level for Part B FFS (check the line first, header as fallback). Avoid trial-and-error column hunting; consult the population matrices.

label: Part D payment composition
definition: Fully costing a Part D prescription requires summing multiple line-level amounts: clm_line_cvrd_pd_amt + clm_line_ncvrd_pd_amt + clm_line_lis_amt + clm_line_othr_tp_pd_amt + clm_line_plro_amt + clm_line_srvc_cst_amt + clm_line_sls_tax_amt. No single payment column represents the total cost of a drug event; which combinations matter depends on the analysis.

label: Partition filter discipline
definition: EDW partitioning relies on clm_type_cd and clm_from_dt, so every claims query should filter both — on each view in a join, not just one side. Predicate effectiveness: equality beats BETWEEN beats NOT IN beats nothing; without a clm_from_dt predicate a query may scan 20+ years of history. Redundant filters across joined views (e.g. the same state constrained on two tables) are encouraged: they cannot change results but reduce the data joined.

label: Provider data sources (NPPES, PECOS, claims systems)
definition: Provider data comes from three systems of record with different grains. NPPES (enumeration — obtaining an NPI) feeds v_prvdr, v_prvdr_hstry, and the v_prvdr_enmrt views: one row per NPI, easiest to join, least current. PECOS (Medicare enrollment) feeds the 30+ v_prvdr_enrlmt-family views: keyed by enrollment id with NPI as a secondary attribute (many rows per NPI), bridged from claims via v_prvdr_mdcr_id. Claims processing systems supply the provider-role columns on the claim views themselves, defined at legacy-ID level. Naming trap: ENMRT = enumeration (NPPES), ENRLMT = enrollment (PECOS).

label: Adjudication-system claim types and record kinds
definition: Within an original claim bundle (see original_claim_bundle) the adjudication streams distinguish claim versions differently. Stream A carries three kinds: the original claim (clm_ctl_num equals the bundle's clm_orig_ctl_num), adjustments (a new clm_ctl_num with clm_adj_type_cd = 2 carrying the original control number), and cancellations (clm_adj_type_cd = 1). Stream B instead carries every processing version as its own row and marks the surviving one with the final-action indicator. Reconstructing a bundle therefore means grouping on the bundle key and ordering by control number and load date; because version semantics differ per stream, a cross-stream query filters to final action (clm_fnl_act_ind = 'Y') rather than reasoning about version kinds.

label: Final action indicator
definition: clm_fnl_act_ind identifies which version of a claim is currently effective. When a claim loads, it is compared to the others in its claim family: the effective version gets 'Y' and superseded versions flip to 'N'; the flags update automatically as new claims load. It works with clm_efctv_dt (when the version became effective) and clm_obslt_dt (when it was superseded; 9999-12-31 = still current). A voided claim with no replacement leaves the family with NO 'Y' row. Final-action rules are stream-specific, and for Medicaid claims the source system (not the EDW) assigns the indicator. Filtering clm_fnl_act_ind = 'Y' is the standard way to select final-action claims, but results drift over time as new loads arrive — see as_is_vs_as_was_reporting.

label: Claim type code
definition: clm_type_cd identifies which source stream and claim type a row in the shared claim views came from - the EDW stores claims from many source feeds in the same tables, so nearly every query filters on it (it also drives partitioning; see partition_filter_discipline). The code's LENGTH and leading digit tell you the stream at a glance: 1 character = drug events; 2 characters = the national claims stream (institutional, professional, and DME sub-ranges); 4 characters starting with 1 or 2 = the adjudication systems, where 1xxx and 2xxx are the early- and final-phase records of the SAME claims (see claim_phases); 4 = encounter; 8 = the Medicaid feed (80xx FFS, 81xx managed-care encounter). The 4-digit codes are composed, and the adjudication and encounter codes compose the same way: for institutional claims the last three digits carry the bill classification (1011 and 4011 are both hospital inpatient - through the adjudication systems and as an encounter respectively), while non-institutional codes use x700 professional, x800 DME, and x900 dental plus stream-specific specials. The full enumeration with per-code attributes lives in the ref.codes.clm_type_cd reference table - concepts teach, ref tables enumerate - and clm_pgm_type_cd (on the v_clm_type_cd reference view) rolls codes up into program families like INST-NCS, INST-ADJ, and PROF-ENC. The Medicaid feed defines its own claim-type logic, so the numbering conventions apply only loosely to the 8xxx codes.
notes: Source: origin-system training material and the source data dictionary.

label: As-is vs. as-was reporting
definition: As-is reporting reflects the data at run time via clm_fnl_act_ind = 'Y'; rerunning later can give different results as adjustments load. The EDW keeps no frozen snapshots, but an as-was result (as of a past date) is closely simulated with predicates: clm_efctv_dt <= as-was date, clm_obslt_dt > as-was date, clm_edw_ld_dt < as-was date, and clm_err_sgntr_sk <> 3. The effective/obsolete pair re-finds the version that was final on that date; the load-date predicate excludes later arrivals. clm_err_sgntr_sk = 3 marks cancelled claims with no replacement whose obsolete date stayed 9999-12-31 — they would otherwise falsely appear to have been final.

label: Claim change actions (correction through voiding)
definition: Five provider actions change a claim after submission, each with a different system consequence. A correction fixes a returned claim in place - no new control number and no new claim row. A resubmission creates a NEW claim with a new control number and no link to the original. An adjustment creates a new version row inside the same bundle (clm_adj_type_cd = 2) carrying the original control number. A cancellation voids a prior version (clm_adj_type_cd = 1). A void-and-rebill pairs a cancellation with a fresh submission, which the bundle key ties back together only when the resubmission carries the original control number. Consequence for analysis: counting rows without filtering to final action overstates claim volume, and any join keyed on control numbers must decide which version kinds it means.

label: Claim family and the effective 4-part key
definition: Claim versions that revise the same service encounter are grouped into a claim family. The effective 4-part key (geo_mbr_efctv_sk, clm_type_efctv_cd, clm_num_efctv_sk, clm_dt_grp_efctv_sk) groups records within the same claim family — filter on it to retrieve all records in the family. The effective keys are EDW-generated and dependably populated, and they apply to every claim stream the EDW aggregates, so they are the preferred family-grouping handle. National-stream and adjudication-system claims additionally carry source-system control numbers that express the same lineage (see original_claim_bundle); those are source-supplied and may not be populated by all source systems.
notes: Source: origin-system training material; maintainer guidance (effective keys apply to all EDW claim streams and are the preferred family-grouping handle).

label: Original claim bundle and claim control numbers
definition: For national-stream and adjudication-system claim types only, claim-family lineage is carried in source-system control numbers alongside the EDW-generated effective keys: an adjusted claim receives a new claim control number (clm_ctl_num) carrying the original control number (clm_orig_ctl_num), and the adjustment type code (clm_adj_type_cd: 0 = original, 1 = credit/cancellation, 2 = replacement) marks each row's role. The original claim bundle expresses this lineage as a grouping recipe: claims sharing mbr_sk, the facility/care type (the last two digits of clm_type_cd), and clm_orig_ctl_num form one bundle, and a claim is a unique clm_ctl_num within its bundle (the original claim's control number equals the bundle's clm_orig_ctl_num). mbr_sk plays the same stable-person role that Warehouse's Person Key plays for OCS claims data. See adj_claim_types_and_records for the claim versions an adjudication-system bundle can contain. Reconstruct bundles by grouping on clm_type (for adjudication-system claims, mapping the 1xxx and 2xxx phase codes to one value), mbr_sk, and clm_orig_ctl_num, then sorting within the group by clm_ctl_num, clm_xref_cncl_doc_ctl_num, clm_phase_cd, clm_efctv_dt, clm_obslt_dt, clm_edw_ld_dt. This approach does not extend to the other streams the EDW aggregates (drug events, encounter, the Medicaid feed): clm_orig_ctl_num comes from the source system that sends the claim and may not be populated — when both handles are available, prefer the effective 4-part key (see claim_family_and_effective_key).
notes: Source: origin-system training material; Warehouse claims reference workbook; maintainer guidance (NCS/Shared-Systems-only scope and control-number reliability).

label: Type of Bill decomposition
definition: The 4-digit institutional Type of Bill is stored as three columns (the leading zero is dropped): clm_bill_fac_type_cd (facility type, e.g. 8 = hospice), clm_bill_clsfctn_cd (bill classification, e.g. inpatient vs RHC), and clm_bill_freq_cd (position in the submission sequence: 0 = nonpayment, 1 = admit-through-discharge, 7 = replacement, G/H/M = OCS/CMS/MSP-initiated adjustments). Code sets are maintained by NUBC; descriptions come from the v_clm_bill_freq_cd reference view joined on all three columns.

label: EDW name abbreviation convention
definition: EDW object names — views, columns, schemas, and databases alike — are English terms with vowels and extra letters removed: INSTNL = Institutional, PRFNL = Professional, DCMTN = Documentation, GRP = Group, SK = Surrogate Key, PMT = Payment, PRCDR = Procedure, ENCTR = Encounter, BLG = Billing, RNDRG = Rendering, PRSBNG = Prescribing, CNTRCTR = Contractor, BENE = Beneficiary, PRVDR = Provider, CLM = Claim, MDCR = Medicare, MDCD = Medicaid.

label: Missing-value sentinels by data type
definition: The EDW encodes "missing" with literal sentinel values rather than NULL alone, and the convention differs by data type. It applies EDW-wide, not just to the claim views, and holds wherever a column is read even where the column's own description does not mention it. CHARACTER columns: a tilde ('~') or NULL means the field does not apply for that claim type or source, while an empty string ('') means it applies but is not populated — three states, and the applies-vs-does-not-apply distinction is real information, not noise. NUMERIC columns: NULL means the field does not apply for that claim type or source, and 0 means the value is genuinely zero. DATE columns: 9999-12-31 marks a still-active or not-yet-superseded row, while 1900-01-01 or NULL means the date is not available or not applicable for that claim type or source.
